category: error tracking and application monitoring (hosted), sponsored plan for open source projects

free_tier.stated: Open-Source Sponsorship Plan, granted on application: 5M errors, 5,000GB logs, 5,000GB application metrics, 1B spans, 100K replays, 500 cron monitors, 25 uptime monitors, 3K continuous profile hours, 150 UI profile hours, 10GB of attachments and 1000 size analysis uploads per month, 5 Seer active contributor seats, Business features, no term limit and no limit on members
free_tier.notes: Counted per event category: errors, spans and replays are event counts; logs, application metrics and attachments are GB; cron and uptime monitors are counts of monitors. The quota is fixed; volume past it needs a pay-as-you-go budget, which needs a credit card on the account.

per_object_cap.stated: Spans are limited to 100KB, the Business plan limit that a help article applies to the sponsored open source plan
per_object_cap.notes: Sentry's size-limits guide, which names no plan, rejects events over 200KB compressed or 1MB decompressed and minidump uploads over 40MB compressed or 200MB decompressed (all files combined).

retention.stated: 30 days for logs and profiles, and 30 days of full-fidelity spans plus 13 months of sampled spans: the Business plan retention that a help article applies to the sponsored open source plan
retention.notes: The retention table gives 90 days for errors on the Business plan; whether the sponsored plan follows that column for errors is unverified.

egress.terms: not stated: the sponsorship pages list ingest quotas only and name no charge for reading data back

interface_detail: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically; the sponsorship pages do not state whether the plan includes API access
tooling: the Sentry SDKs, the Sentry web API and the Sentry web app
chaining: An error, trace and cron check-in sink for jobs on free or rented compute: 500 cron monitors and 1B spans a month, with Business features and no term limit, for a project that passes the sponsorship review.

limits.value: an application is reviewed by Sentry support and sponsorships are granted at Sentry's discretion; the project should be released under a friendly licence such as Apache or MIT, one organization is sponsored, and a social enterprise or B-Corp that makes a profit does not qualify
5M errors, 1B spans and 100K replays per month; events past the quota are dropped unless a pay-as-you-go budget is added, and the base quota cannot be adjusted
5,000GB of logs, 5,000GB of application metrics and 10GB of attachments per month

limits_note: 500 cron monitors, 25 uptime monitors, 3K continuous profile hours, 150 UI profile hours and 1000 size analysis uploads per month, 5 Seer active contributor seats and Business features, which the plan page does not enumerate. A legacy sponsored plan, assigned before the current feature set, does not show the Business features until support migrates it to the latest plan on request.
binding_note: A support review at Sentry's discretion comes before any quota applies; once granted, 5M errors a month is the first volume ceiling, and new events are refused past it until the next usage period unless a pay-as-you-go budget is added.

identity_cost.detail: A Sentry organization comes first: the sign-up form asks for name, organization, email and password behind a reCAPTCHA. The sponsorship application names that organization and asks for website URL, company type, project URL, a GitHub link to the licence where available and a description; support reviews it and names the documentation it requires (unverified: behind a sign-up and an application). The sign-up form and the application have no card field; pay-as-you-go spend past the quota is enabled by adding a credit card to the account.

reliability_note: events past the quota are dropped and cannot be recovered, even after a pay-as-you-go budget is enabled; the base quota of a sponsored plan cannot be adjusted
